items.title: Does Lyft (LYFT) Merit A Discount After Its Driver Rewards Deal?
items.summary: Lyft shares closed at US$16.14 after a mixed run that includes a sharp decline over the past five years, and the question now is whether that price still lines up with what the company is earning. Recent stock swings and fresh partnership news put the focus squarely on how much of Lyft’s current valuation can be explained by its profit potential. items.title: Bernstein’s $250 Target Says DoorDash’s Selloff Went Too Far
items.summary: Key TakeawaysDoorDash stock is 31% below its August high after Amazon gave Prime members free Uber Eats delivery and the Justice Department reportedly moved to review DoorDash’s Instacart deal. Bernstein cut its DoorDash target to $250 from $270 and kept its Outperform rating, a target 53% above the stock.

items.title: Should You Buy Uber Stock For Its Cash?
items.summary: Uber Technologies produced free cash flow equal to 8% of its market value at Monday's close. The median S&P 500 company stood at 4.4%. Free cash flow is the cash left from operations after spending on equipment and property. For Uber, it came to $10.4 billion in the twelve months to September.

items.title: Trump’s Labor Department Just Made It Easier to Treat Drivers as Contractors. That’s Good News for Uber
items.summary: Key TakeawaysThe Labor Department finalized a rule, effective in January, that makes it easier to classify workers as independent contractors. That lowers the federal risk that Uber (UBER:NYSE), DoorDash (DASH:NASDAQ), and Lyft (LYFT:NASDAQ) must treat drivers as employees, who can cost up to 30% more.
